# The model

A count [outcome](model-validation.qmd#def-outcome-vector),
such as the number of bike rentals in an hour,
is not well described by a [normal distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-normal)
when the counts are small,
since the normal distribution puts [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) below zero,
and a count is never below zero.
A [Poisson regression model](poisson-regression.qmd#def-poisson-regression) takes the [event rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-event-rate)
to be the [exponential function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-exponential-function) of a [linear function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-linear-function) of the [covariates](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate).
